extracted.intended_audience: federal agency SBIR/STTR program managers, SBA analysts, and policymakers overseeing SBIR/STTR compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing whether Participating Agencies met statutory SBIR/STTR minimum spending requirements by comparing obligated SBIR/STTR dollars to agencies' reported extramural R/R&D obligations (as reported to SBA and to NCSES), accounting for exemptions, reporting basis, and timing differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory definition of 'extramural budget' (15 U.S.C. § 638(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: [T]he sum of the total obligations [for R/R&D] minus amounts obligated for such activities by employees of the agency in or through Government-owned, Government-operated facilities, except that for the Department of Energy it shall not include amounts obligated for atomic energy defense programs solely for weapons activities or for naval reactor programs, and except that for the Agency for International Development it shall not include amounts obligated solely for general institutional support of international research centers or for grants to foreign countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this statutory definition as the basis for calculating an agency's extramural R/R&D budget; note the explicit exceptions for DOE and USAID when determining what to include/exclude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement to NCSES (NCSES Survey)
rubrics_metrics.description: As prescribed in Section 10(h)(4)(iv) of the SBIR/STTR Policy Directive, Participating Agencies must report the total fiscal year extramural R/R&D obligations as reported to the U.S. National Science Foundation (NCSES Survey).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA compares NCSES Survey results to agency submissions to SBA; agencies must provide a rationale for any variance between amounts reported to SBA and amounts reported to NCSES. When provided, agency explanations are included in the SBA report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary assessment measures (two-measure approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA assesses compliance through two measures: 1) percentage of funding obligated for SBIR/STTR activities divided by total extramural R/R&D obligations minus program exemptions as reported to SBA; and 2) percentage of funding obligated for SBIR/STTR activities based on total extramural R/R&D obligations reported by the Agency to NCSES minus the amount of program exemptions reported to SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an agency's NCSES total is lower than SBA's reported total, the calculated SBIR/STTR percentages based on NCSES will be higher, and vice versa; SBA uses both measures in its compliance determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance rubric — Complied
rubrics_metrics.description: Complied: Agency must have obligated at least 3.2% for SBIR and .45% for STTR of its total extramural R/R&D obligations as reported to SBA, and the R/R&D obligations reported to NCSES are not significantly more (<15%) than what was reported to SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the percentage thresholds and NCSES variance check must be satisfied for a 'Complied' determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance rubric — Did Not Comply
rubrics_metrics.description: Did Not Comply: Agency is not compliant if it reports obligating less than the respective percentages (3.2% for SBIR and .45% for STTR) of its total extramural R/R&D obligations as reported to SBA, or the R/R&D obligations reported to NCSES are significantly more (>15%) than the extramural R/R&D obligations reported to SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either failure to meet the percentage threshold OR a >15% upward variance in NCSES vs SBA reporting is sufficient to label an agency 'Did Not Comply.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance rubric — Unable to Determine
rubrics_metrics.description: Unable to Determine: SBA is unable to determine compliance because SBA cannot validate the agency's exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when exemptions (amounts excluded from extramural calculations) reported by an agency cannot be verified by SBA; leads to inability to conclude compliance status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum percentage thresholds for SBIR and STTR
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory minimum set-aside rates: 3.2% for SBIR and 0.45% for STTR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exact percentages are the baseline quantitative criteria applied to calculated obligations for compliance measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCSES vs SBA variance significance threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA treats NCSES-reported extramural R/R&D obligations as 'significantly more' when they are >15% higher than amounts reported to SBA; 'not significantly more' is defined as <15%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 15% variance cutoff is explicitly used in the compliance rubric to decide whether differences between data sources affect compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting basis: Obligations (O) vs Appropriations (A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies report extramural R/R&D to SBA either as obligations (O) or appropriations (A); DoD reports appropriations rather than actual obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA flags reporting differences because appropriations-based reporting (as by DoD) can prevent SBA from validating whether the agency met the minimum spending requirement in the fiscal year; explanatory narrative and component-level breakdowns are used to address this limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe to obligate allocated funding (funding availability periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies have differing funding availability (1-year, 2-year, no-year, multi-year), which affects the year in which appropriated funds can be obligated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA measures what was obligated in the current fiscal year regardless of when funds were set aside; for two-year/no-year authorities (e.g., DoD), obligated amounts may occur in later years, complicating single-year compliance determinations. DoD may achieve compliance at the end of its two-year execution window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program exemptions and treatment in calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Agencies may report 'Amount of Program Exemptions' to exclude certain dollars from extramural R/R&D calculations (e.g., intramural costs, payroll, travel, facilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA subtracts reported exemptions from total extramural obligations when computing denominators; SBA must validate exemptions or else conclude 'Unable to Determine.' Examples: NASA and EPA use different methodologies for exclusions, producing reconciliation differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NCSES Survey as comparison and known measurement caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: NCSES (NSF) administers the Survey of Federal Funds for Research and Development as a census and provides data used for comparison, but NSF indicates 'some measurement problems known to exist' in the Survey data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA uses NCSES data to identify compliance issues but acknowledges methodological differences between NCSES and SBA SBIR reporting (e.g., NCSES may report enacted budget levels while SBA reports actual obligations), which can cause non-reconcilable differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate analysis for Civilian agencies and DoD components (delineation requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA reports on how civilian and defense agencies met minimum spending requirements separately, and further delineates DoD data by Service Components and Other Defense Agencies for more detailed review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This separation and component-level breakdown improves transparency and enables targeted analysis of compliance by organizational unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency explanation requirement for variances
rubrics_metrics.description: When extramural R/R&D obligations reported to NCSES differ from amounts reported to SBA, SBA requested Participating Agencies provide a rationale for any variance; agency explanations are included when provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should document methodological differences, timing/appropriation considerations, and specific categories excluded to support reconciliation; SBA includes those explanations in its report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective treatment of appropriations across fiscal years (DoD example)
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD retrospective: appropriations for a fiscal year are often obligated across that year and the subsequent year (RDT&E two-year availability), so DoD may execute authorized SBIR/STTR funding over two years and achieve compliance at the end of that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA may perform retrospectives tracking obligations by year-of-appropriation vs year-of-obligation (e.g., FY21 appropriation obligated in FY21 and FY22) to reassess compliance once obligations have exhausted their multi-year availability.
